author: San Antonio Standard
title: Rep. Pat Fallon addresses DHS shutdown and national security concerns in March tweets
text:
Rep. Pat Fallon, who represents Texas’s 4th district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of tweets in mid-March 2026 addressing issues related to national security, immigration policy, and authoritarian regimes.
On March 16, 2026, Fallon criticized congressional Democrats for their stance on Department of Homeland Security operations: “Democrats have shut down DHS for a month now because they prioritize criminal illegals over the safety of American citizens. Democrats can simply come to the table and reopen DHS, but they are terrified of their far-left base.”
The following day, March 17, he advocated for enhanced cyber defense capabilities: “A dedicated US Cyber Force is critical to deterring future threats from adversaries. US national security can’t wait. Looking forward to the discussion tomorrow with @CSIS.”
Later that same day, Fallon referenced several countries as examples of authoritarianism: “*Worst case scenario for authoritarianism. Venezuela, Iran, Cuba–all authoritarian regimes that rig elections and punish dissent.”
Fallon has represented Texas’s 4th district since 2021 after succeeding John Ratcliffe and previously served in both chambers of the Texas Legislature. He was born in Pittsfield, Massachusetts in 1967 and currently resides in Frisco at age 55. In recent election cycles, Fallon has maintained significant electoral margins against his opponents; he won re-election in 2024 with more than two-thirds of the vote against Simon Cardell.
